result: Explicit user instruction restores uptake to 15/20 with a fully working deliberation loop.

quiz_readership.finding: Every controller, including Ling, correctly states the caller observes nothing of a deliberate-alone turn and the proxy resumes with a checkpoint. The injected system prompt is read and understood by all five. Non-use was never a comprehension failure.

compliance.non_compliant: 5 requests acted directly without deliberating (zen-early-r1, cf-super-late x2, ling-late x2)

interpretation: The full v4 loop works end to end on live models: focus question asked, four usable continuations, accepted reduction, valid outward action.
Selection, not comprehension, is the blocker: models know exactly how the tool works and still never volunteer it; a direct user instruction flips 0% spontaneous uptake to 75% compliance.
System-prompt placement is the likely salience gap: identical content as a user message is obeyed; as an injected system note it never surfaces during task work.
Compliance is instruction-following, NOT spontaneous uptake. These rows must never be pooled with uptake arms or cited as spontaneous use.
Strategic consequence: a harness-level deliberation instruction is a viable integration path, but it is a different condition from the published same-harness baseline and must be evaluated as such.
